feature: Sec-Agent-Workspace — PII Scanner & Intelligent Audit System

tasks.title: Install and configure core dependencies
tasks.description: Install all required packages: shadcn/ui (with its CLI init), framer-motion, zustand, prisma + @prisma/client, bullmq, ioredis, ai (Vercel AI SDK), playwright. Also add @types/ioredis and other missing dev types. Run `pnpm dlx shadcn@latest init` to scaffold shadcn config (components.json, updated tailwind config, cn utility). Update package.json scripts to add `check:types` (tsc --noEmit).
acceptance_criteria: `pnpm install` completes without errors
`pnpm check:types` passes with zero errors on the bare scaffold
`components.json` exists and references the correct tailwind config
`lib/utils.ts` exports a `cn` helper using clsx + tailwind-merge

tasks.title: Define Prisma schema and push to SQLite
tasks.description: Create `prisma/schema.prisma` with the SQLite datasource and two models: ScanTask (id, targetUrl, status, createdAt, updatedAt) and Vulnerability (id, taskId, url, field, riskLevel, reasoning, confidence, rawData, createdAt). Run `pnpx prisma db push` to create the local SQLite file. Export a singleton Prisma client from `lib/db.ts`.
acceptance_criteria: `prisma/schema.prisma` contains both ScanTask and Vulnerability models with all fields from the PRD

tasks.title: Build Zustand store with all state fields and actions

Define all supporting TypeScript types in `lib/types.ts`. Include actions: `addLog`, `addRisk`, `setLiveFrame`, `setTelemetry`, `upsertSitemapNode`, `setScanStatus`, `reset`.
acceptance_criteria: `lib/types.ts` exports LogEntry, RiskEntry, TelemetryStatus, SitemapNode, ScanStatus with no `any` types
`lib/store.ts` imports only from zustand and lib/types — zero Node.js native imports

All six state fields and all seven actions are present and correctly typed

tasks.title: Implement SSE API route /api/events
tasks.description: Create `app/api/events/route.ts` as a Next.js Route Handler that returns a streaming `Response` with `Content-Type: text/event-stream`. Subscribe to a Redis Pub/Sub channel (`scan-events`) using a dedicated ioredis subscriber client. For each message received, parse the JSON payload and forward it as an SSE event (`data: ...\n\n`). Handle client disconnect by unsubscribing and closing the Redis connection. Support all seven SSE event types from the PRD (LOG, RISK, FRAME, AUTH_REQUIRED, TELEMETRY, SITEMAP, SCAN_DONE).
acceptance_criteria: GET /api/events returns Content-Type: text/event-stream
Messages published to the `scan-events` Redis channel appear as SSE events within 500ms
Client disconnect triggers cleanup (unsubscribe + Redis connection close) without unhandled promise rejections
`pnpm check:types` passes

tasks.title: Implement POST /api/scan/start and POST /api/scan/stop
tasks.description: Create `app/api/scan/start/route.ts`: validate the `targetUrl` body field, create a ScanTask record in Prisma with status `running`, enqueue a BullMQ job with the taskId and targetUrl, return `{ taskId }`. Create `app/api/scan/stop/route.ts`: accept `{ taskId }`, update the ScanTask status to `failed` in Prisma, drain/remove the matching BullMQ job, publish a SCAN_DONE event to Redis. Both routes must wrap all logic in try-catch and return appropriate HTTP error responses.
acceptance_criteria: POST /api/scan/start with a valid URL returns 200 with `{ taskId }` and creates a DB record
POST /api/scan/start with a missing URL returns 400
POST /api/scan/stop updates the DB record status to `failed`
Both routes return 500 with an error message on unexpected failures
`pnpm check:types` passes

tasks.title: Build the standalone BullMQ Worker process
tasks.description: Create `worker/index.ts` as a standalone Node.js script (not a Next.js route). It registers a BullMQ Worker on the `scan-queue`. The job handler receives `{ taskId, targetUrl }`, launches a Playwright Chromium browser, navigates to the target URL, takes a screenshot, encodes it as base64, and publishes a FRAME event to Redis. Also publish a LOG event for each major step. Wrap all Playwright calls in try-catch; on error publish a LOG event with level `error` and update the ScanTask status to `failed` in Prisma. Add a `worker` script to package.json: `ts-node worker/index.ts`.
acceptance_criteria: `worker/index.ts` starts without import errors when run with `pnpm worker`
Processing a job publishes at least one LOG event and one FRAME event to Redis
A Playwright error is caught, logged as an error-level LOG event, and does not crash the worker process
The ScanTask DB record is updated to `completed` on success and `failed` on error
`pnpm check:types` passes for worker/index.ts

Mount this hook in `components/providers.tsx`. Add a URL input form to `app/page.tsx` that calls POST /api/scan/start and sets scanStatus to 'running' in the store.
acceptance_criteria: Opening the app establishes an EventSource connection to /api/events (visible in browser DevTools Network tab)

tasks.title: Integrate Vercel AI SDK with DOM-reading agent tools
tasks.description: In `worker/agent.ts`, implement the AI agent loop using Vercel AI SDK `generateText` with `tools`. Define two tools: `read_dom` (takes no args, returns the current page's simplified DOM as a string via `page.evaluate`) and `explore_menu` (takes a CSS selector, clicks it, waits for navigation/expansion, returns updated DOM). The agent loop runs until the AI returns no more tool calls or a max-step limit is reached. Publish a TELEMETRY event with `{ capability: 'AI DOM Parsing', active: true }` when the loop starts.

tasks.title: Implement human-in-the-loop authentication flow
tasks.description: In `worker/agent.ts`, add login detection: after `read_dom`, check if the DOM contains a password input field. If detected: publish AUTH_REQUIRED event with the current page URL, pause the BullMQ job (or block on a Redis key), and publish TELEMETRY `{ capability: 'Auto-Login Detection', active: true }`. Create `app/api/worker/resume/route.ts` (POST): accept `{ taskId, username, password }`, store credentials in a Redis key (`auth:{taskId}`), and signal the worker to resume. In the worker, poll for the Redis key, then call `page.fill()` for username and password fields and submit the form.

POST /api/worker/resume stores credentials in Redis and returns 200
After resume, the worker fills the login form and submits it without crashing

`pnpm check:types` passes

tasks.title: Implement Tier 1 Regex network traffic interceptor
tasks.description: In `worker/interceptor.ts`, implement the Tier 1 interceptor. Register `page.on('response', handler)` in the worker. For each response with Content-Type containing `application/json`, read the response body and run a set of regex patterns against it to detect PII signals: email addresses, phone numbers, ID card numbers, credit card patterns, tokens/passwords (fields named `password`, `token`, `secret`, `key`). If any pattern matches, extract the matching JSON snippet and emit it to a callback for Tier 2 processing. Publish a TELEMETRY event `{ capability: 'Deep Intercepting', active: true }` when the interceptor is registered.
acceptance_criteria: `worker/interceptor.ts` exports a `registerInterceptor(page, onMatch, publishEvent)` function
JSON responses containing email addresses are detected by the regex tier
JSON responses containing a field named `password` are detected
Non-JSON responses are silently skipped
TELEMETRY Deep Intercepting event is published on registration
`pnpm check:types` passes

tasks.title: Implement Tier 2 AI semantic vulnerability judgment
tasks.description: In `worker/analyzer.ts`, implement the Tier 2 AI judgment. The `analyzeSnippet(snippet: string, url: string, taskId: string, publishEvent)` function sends the JSON snippet and URL to the AI model via Vercel AI SDK `generateText` with a structured prompt asking it to: determine if real PII is present, identify the field name, assign a risk level (critical/high/medium/low), provide reasoning, and give a confidence score (0-1). Parse the AI response into a `RiskEntry`. Persist the finding to Prisma as a Vulnerability record. Publish a RISK SSE event with the structured data.

The function returns a structured RiskEntry with all required fields (no `any` types)
A Vulnerability record is created in the Prisma DB for each confirmed finding

AI errors are caught and logged as error-level LOG events without crashing
`pnpm check:types` passes

tasks.title: Create captcha detection and handling module
tasks.description: Create `worker/captcha.ts` exporting `detectAndHandleCaptcha(page, taskId, publishEvent)`. Detection logic: scan the DOM for known captcha signals — `img[src*='captcha']`, `canvas`, `.slide-verify`, `.el-slider`, `input[placeholder*='验证码']`, `input[placeholder*='code']`, etc. Classify type: 'image' (static img/canvas captcha), 'slider' (drag-to-verify), 'sms' (phone input + code field), 'email' (email input + code field), 'unknown' (code input present but unclassified). Handling per type: (1) image — screenshot the captcha element via `page.locator(selector).screenshot()`, send to AI Vision via OpenAI-compatible API with prompt 'What text is shown in this captcha image? Reply with only the characters.', fill the input, submit, check for error indicators, retry up to 3 times; (2) slider — use `page.mouse` to simulate a human drag: start at handle, move right in small increments with random ±2px Y jitter and non-uniform speed (Math.random delays), release at track end; (3) sms/email/unknown — publish AUTH_REQUIRED event with captchaType and captchaImageBase64 if available, then poll Redis key `captcha:{taskId}` for the user-submitted code (same pattern as auth credential polling), fill the code input and submit. Returns `{ handled: boolean; captchaType: CaptchaType }`.
acceptance_criteria: `worker/captcha.ts` exports `detectAndHandleCaptcha` with signature `(page: Page, taskId: string, publishEvent: (e: object) => Promise<void>) => Promise<{ handled: boolean; captchaType: CaptchaType }>`
Image captcha path: locates captcha img/canvas, calls AI Vision API, fills input — verified by unit-level inspection of the function
Slider path: uses `page.mouse.move` with at least 10 incremental steps and random Y jitter — no single large jump
SMS/email path: publishes AUTH_REQUIRED with `captchaType` and optional `captchaImageBase64`, polls `captcha:{taskId}` Redis key
`pnpm check:types` passes with no `any` types

tasks.title: Extend AUTH_REQUIRED event type and resume API

Update `app/api/worker/resume/route.ts` to accept an optional `captchaCode?: string` field in the request body alongside `username` and `password`. If `captchaCode` is present, store it in Redis key `captcha:{taskId}` (in addition to or instead of the auth key, depending on which fields are non-empty). Update `hooks/use-sse.ts` to extract `captchaType` and `captchaImageBase64` from AUTH_REQUIRED events and store them via two new store actions.
acceptance_criteria: `CaptchaType` and `AuthRequiredEvent` are exported from `lib/types.ts` with no `any`
POST /api/worker/resume with `{ taskId, captchaCode: '1234' }` stores `captcha:{taskId}` = '1234' in Redis and returns 200
POST /api/worker/resume still handles `{ taskId, username, password }` correctly (backwards compatible)
`lib/store.ts` has `captchaType: CaptchaType | null` and `captchaImageBase64: string | null` state fields with setter actions
`pnpm check:types` passes

tasks.title: Extend AuthModal with captcha-aware UI
tasks.description: Update `components/auth-modal.tsx` to render different UI based on `captchaType` from the Zustand store. Layout: the modal always shows the `pageUrl`. Then conditionally: (1) `captchaType === 'image'` — show the captcha image (``) and a single code input labeled 'Captcha Text'; also show username/password fields since image captchas usually accompany a login form; (2) `captchaType === 'sms'` — show message 'A verification code was sent to your phone. Enter it below.' + code input only; (3) `captchaType === 'email'` — same but 'check your email'; (4) `captchaType === 'slider'` — show 'Auto-handling slider captcha...' spinner with a Framer Motion animated indicator, no input needed, modal auto-closes when scanStatus returns to 'running'; (5) `captchaType === 'unknown'` or null — show username/password + optional code input (current behavior). On submit, POST to `/api/worker/resume` with whichever fields are filled (username, password, captchaCode).
acceptance_criteria: Modal renders captcha image when `captchaType === 'image'` and `captchaImageBase64` is set
Modal shows SMS-specific message and only a code input when `captchaType === 'sms'`
Modal shows animated spinner (Framer Motion) and no inputs when `captchaType === 'slider'`

`pnpm check:types` passes, no `any` types

tasks.title: Wire captcha module into the agent flow
tasks.description: Update `worker/agent.ts`: in `handleAuthIfNeeded`, call `detectAndHandleCaptcha(page, taskId, publishEvent)` BEFORE checking for password inputs. If `detectAndHandleCaptcha` returns `{ handled: true }` and the captcha type was 'slider' (auto-handled), wait 2s then re-check the page — if it navigated away from the login page, return early (no further auth needed). If captcha was sms/email/unknown (human handled), after the user submits the code, re-run the password fill logic to complete login. If `detectAndHandleCaptcha` returns `{ handled: false }`, fall through to the existing password-fill logic unchanged. No changes to `worker/index.ts` needed since `runAgent` already calls `handleAuthIfNeeded` internally.
acceptance_criteria: `detectAndHandleCaptcha` is called at the top of `handleAuthIfNeeded` before password detection
When captcha type is 'slider' and handled successfully, the function returns without triggering AUTH_REQUIRED
When captcha type is 'sms' and user submits code, the agent proceeds to fill password fields afterwards
If no captcha is detected, existing password-fill behaviour is unchanged
`pnpm check:types` passes
